warnings: This paper studies SEED zinc content effects, NOT zinc fertilizer application - may not be relevant for the meta-analysis
The main treatment is different seed Zn contents (355, 800, 1465 ng Zn seed-1), not fertilizer application
Soil Zn application is a secondary factor (23 kg Zn ha-1 vs 0 kg Zn ha-1)
Table 2 only shows Zn concentrations for rainfed conditions, irrigated data not presented
Grain Zn concentration data is very limited - only in Table 2 with no variance measures provided
The paper focuses more on yield effects than Zn biofortification

recon.variance_source: LSD(5%) values are provided in Table 1 for yield data, described as 'LSD(5%) =' with significance indicators
recon.control_definition: Seeds with 355 ng Zn seed-1 content grown without soil Zn application (0 kg Zn ha-1)
recon.treatment_definition: Seeds with higher Zn content (800 or 1465 ng Zn seed-1) and/or soil Zn application (23 kg Zn ha-1)
recon.potential_tc_confusion: This paper studies seed Zn content as primary factor, not fertilizer application - may not fit meta-analysis scope
recon.sample_size_source: Experimental design was a two-factor randomized complete block design in split plots with six replications
recon.factorial_structure: ["seed Zn content (3 levels)", "soil Zn application (2 levels)", "irrigation (2 levels)", "year (2 levels)"]
recon.extraction_guidance: WARNING: This paper may not be suitable for the meta-analysis as it primarily studies seed Zn content effects rather than fertilizer application. If extracting, use Table 2 for grain Zn concentrations, compare soil Zn application effects (0 vs 23 kg Zn ha-1) within each seed Zn content level. No variance measures provided for Zn concentration data. Data only available for rainfed conditions.
